read_scope.notes: Read the complete 22-page frozen PDF, including references and Appendices A-G, using page-separated text extraction, and visually inspected every rendered page. Inspected all six figures and all nine tables. Consulted frozen paper.tex and specificity_results.tex for exact wording, notation and locations. Technical appendix derivations were treated as optional depth when judging main-text accessibility. Independently computed the supplied PDF SHA256. No other review records, drafts, progress records, goals, external sources or non-snapshot manuscript were consulted. Abstract has 145 whitespace-delimited words in the supplied TeX.

score_reasons.expression: Precise, fluent prose usually states the interpretation before the qualification. The warm-every-image example and the zero/matched/doubled-contrast example in Section 4.1 make difficult distinctions economical and memorable. Result headings state findings rather than analysis names. Local friction remains in the abstract's unconditional noise-bias wording and in the compressed diagnostic language at the ends of Sections 5.4-5.5; these need targeted replacements, not broad rewriting.
score_reasons.structure: The main text has an excellent question-to-design-to-measurement-to-results progression. Section 4.1 supplies intuition before the equations, Section 4.4 establishes the retrospective status of additional comparisons, and Sections 5.1-5.5 develop response detection, shared change, pair coverage, calibration and source dependence in a coherent sequence. Optional estimator details and earlier cohorts are kept in appendices. One float interrupts the opening of Section 5.2, and the final control summary in Section 5.5 would be better left to its appendix.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The prompt arms, reference collection, equal painter weighting, feature units and no-contrast benchmark are recoverable without the repository. Tables 1-3 and the Figure 2/3 reading instructions explain how to interpret the main numbers. The main text also clearly distinguishes a feature-space calibration from an image improvement. Accessibility is slightly weakened when two different directional alignment ratios appear without their benchmarks or a clear distinction from beta, and when the last paragraph of Section 5.5 introduces an unexplained 11-brief subset and split-reference controls.
score_reasons.engagement: The opening Monet-Sisley example poses a consequential evaluation question without hype. The consistent scene gallery, labeled-pattern plot and pair heatmaps reward inspection, while GPT Image 2's near-unit slope but substantial error and the two ordering reversals provide a clear narrative. Momentum weakens briefly when Section 5.5 compresses several different diagnostic stories into its final paragraph, and the Figure 2 float separates the shared-effect result from its interpretation.

strengths: Section 4.1, page 5, explains why no painter distinctions, exact reference contrasts and doubled contrasts have expected errors 1, 0 and 1. This is a particularly effective bridge from the research question to the estimator.

Sections 3.1-3.3, pages 2-3, define a finite digital target, development-panel scaling and the actual meaning of color, spatial and texture features. Table 1 keeps these measurements interpretable without pretending to validate artistic style.

Section 5.1 and Table 2, pages 6-7, separate positive aligned response, model-pair comparisons and the unresolved no-contrast benchmark. The text explicitly warns that the Sunburst comparison changes under source correction.
Figure 1, page 4, consistently holds the scene across models and painter names; Figures 2 and 3, pages 7-8, give explicit instructions for reading the plotted contrasts and pair scores.
Section 5.4 and Table 3, page 9, explain both calibration and scene-averaging order changes in concrete model comparisons, with clear limits on what either operation demonstrates.

The manuscript repeatedly and accurately identifies retrospective diagnostics, approximate inference and the limits of reference corrections. The earlier contrary transfer result and pixel-access limitation remain visible without displacing the main experiment.

findings.location: Abstract, page 1; paper.tex lines 33-35, compared with Section 4.2, page 5, and Appendix C.4, pages 17-18
findings.issue: The standalone abstract says that independent-repeat products estimate disagreement "without sampling-noise bias." The main text correctly makes this conditional on stable conditional means and independent, mean-zero repeat errors, and explicitly says that separate requests do not establish service independence. The abstract presents the ideal property too categorically for that stated limitation.
findings.reader_effect: An abstract-only reader can mistake a conditional estimator property for an empirically established absence of noise bias in these collected outputs.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the clause with "repeat products correct noise bias under stable-mean and independence assumptions." This is a local wording change and fits within the 155-word abstract limit; retain the fuller qualifications in Section 4.2.

findings.location: Section 5.2, page 8, and Section 5.4, page 9; specificity_results.tex lines 48-52 and 89-94
findings.issue: The results introduce "cross-repeat alignment ratios" for generic versus common named shifts, then "the highest corrected alignment ratio" for generated versus reference contrasts. Neither passage tells the main-text reader how these directional ratios differ from the already defined aligned response beta. The latter ratio's numerical value and definition appear only in Table 6 and Appendix B.1.
findings.reader_effect: Because all three quantities are called alignment, a reader may treat the new ratios as beta, or regard them as directly comparable measures of the same relationship. This blurs the reason shrinking a response with beta near one can help.
findings.suggested_change: Name the compared directions and the purpose of each ratio in the existing sentences. For Section 5.2, say that the generic and common named shifts have similar directions, with an ideal directional ratio of one for parallel shifts, but that generic shifts are smaller. In Section 5.4, replace the unexplained phrase with "After separating direction from size, GPT Image 2 has the strongest directional agreement with the reference contrasts." Keep the formulas and finite-sample caveats in the appendix rather than adding a new main-text derivation.

findings.location: Final paragraph of Section 5.5, page 10; specificity_results.tex lines 139-146
findings.issue: "The same 11 water, built and land briefs" has no earlier main-text introduction explaining the reduction from 14 scenes. The paragraph then introduces "disjoint real-painting controls" and a sparse-sampling explanation without saying what those controls sampled. The relevant explanation is clear in Appendix C.1, but the compressed main-text summary briefly asks the reader to reconstruct a separate design.
findings.reader_effect: The source-correction result loses momentum just before the discussion, and readers may not know whether the 11 scenes or the real-painting controls change the primary experimental panel.
findings.suggested_change: Specify "the 11 water, built and land briefs, excluding the three mixed briefs" and state that the visual-class check replaces the title-derived labels. Move the two real-painting-control sentences entirely to Appendix C.1, where the procedure and its limits are already presented. This preserves evidence while shortening the main text.

findings.location: Figure 2 and opening of Section 5.2, page 7 continuing on page 8
findings.issue: Figure 2 belongs to the preceding explanation of labeled painter geometry, but it floats beneath the Section 5.2 heading and splits its opening paragraph after "These are shares of." The continuation identifying squared feature change appears on the next page.
findings.reader_effect: The reader encounters a large plot about painter contrasts while starting the distinct shared-response result, and the important interpretation of the percentage range is separated from the numbers.
findings.suggested_change: Adjust float placement so Figure 2 precedes the Section 5.2 heading, or move the heading and complete opening paragraph together after the figure. Preserve the existing figure size and the 22-page limit through placement or a small local prose trim.

claim_fidelity_issues: The abstract's "without sampling-noise bias" is too unconditional relative to the stable-mean and repeat-independence assumptions stated in Section 4.2. This is a localized abstract wording issue; the main text adequately qualifies the estimator and inference. No unsupported claim of perceptual artistic fidelity or demonstrated image improvement was identified.
summary: A strong manuscript approaching excellent communication for the specified graduate-level reader. Its main question, experiment, score interpretation and principal findings stand alone, and its technical appendices are appropriately optional. Four localized edits would improve abstract fidelity, metric terminology and result pacing without new evidence or increased length.
